tellings.difference: This telling names the University of Colorado Boulder as where the committee worked, calls the study an outright "hit job", credits the Condon Report, and runs the dates to 1969.
tellings.link_reason: Both are Jesse Michels's tellings of the Condon Committee, the 1966–1968/69 UFO study program, and both credit Edward Condon and Robert Hippler. Calling it a "hit job" fits with the story's claim that the Air Force paid for and steered the committee rather than contradicting it.

as_told.title: Condon Committee hit job at University of Colorado

tellings.quote: The contract provided that the planning, direction and conclusions of the Colorado project were to be conducted wholly independently of the Air Force. To avoid duplication of effort, the Air Force was ordered to furnish the project with the records of its own earlier work and to provide the support of personnel at AF bases when requested by our field teams.
The first research contract with AFOSR provided $313,000 for the first 15 months from 1 November 1966 to 31 January 1968.

plain: In 1966 the Air Force paid the University of Colorado to run an outside scientific study of UFOs, led by Edward Condon, and Michels says that study was not as independent as it claimed. He tells it himself on two episodes: the study was 'paid for, but supposed to be uninfluenced by the Air Force,' and in the end Condon did 'an absolute hit job' on the subject, with one telling running the dates to 1969. The final report, Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects, dated 31 October 1968, says the first contract with the Air Force Office of Scientific Research 'provided $313,000 for the first 15 months.' It says the project's 'planning, direction and conclusions' were to be 'conducted wholly independently of the Air Force,' while the Air Force was ordered to hand over its old records and lend staff at its bases when the field teams asked. So the report itself sets out money and working ties to the Air Force. Any coordination beyond that is Michels's reading, which the report neither states nor rules out. If he is right, the study that closed the official book on UFOs was steered by the service it was meant to check.

discussion.by: Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects (the Condon report, 1968)
discussion.text: The report says the Air Force paid for the project ("The first research contract with AFOSR provided $313,000 for the first 15 months"), that the contract provided that its "planning, direction and conclusions" were to be "conducted wholly independently of the Air Force", and that "the Air Force was ordered to furnish the project with the records of its own earlier work and to provide the support of personnel at AF bases when requested by our field teams", a working tie the report itself sets out. Coordination beyond that is the tellers' reading, which the report neither states nor excludes.
